newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TWO S.AFRICAN INTEREST RATE CUTS SEEN THIS YEAR.
newsitem.headline: TWO S.AFRICAN INTEREST RATE CUTS SEEN THIS YEAR.

text.p: Economists are sounding more upbeat on interest rate cuts this year with Sanlam Asset Management chief economist Jac Laubscher on Friday predicting two cuts still likely in the second half.

Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals last week appeared to throw cold water on expectations of rate cuts this year because of high levels of credit extension, but several economists are now starting to see room for manoeuvre.
Earlier this week Board of Executor's Rob Lee said that an interest rate cut was still possible this year with another two in 1998.

In his forecast, Laubscher said he was not too concerned about continued high levels of private sector credit extension because it appeared to have been fuelled by structural factors that would ease in due course.
"One of these is the switch from foreign credit to local credit which we suspect is taking place in the corporate sector," he said.
This followed the Reserve Bank's withdrawal from the rand forward cover market, which had increased the cost of forward cover.
"We believe that this adjustment has almost run its course and that the growth in credit extension will therefore start to fall at quite a speedy rate in the second quarter of 1997," Laubscher said.
The continuous downward trend in imports of machinery and equipment in March 1997 supported that view.
"(We are) thus of the opinion that conditions will be more favourable for a reduction in short-term interest rates in the second half of 1997," Laubscher said.
He forecast a reduction of one percentage point in the bank rate in the third quarter of 1997, followed by a similar cut in the fourth quarter.
South Africa's prime interest rate currently stands at 20.25 percent while the bank rate is 17 percent.
Inflation was expected to peak at just below 10 percent in April and fall to 7.6 percent by the end of the year, Laubscher added.
